f.title: Use an alternative approach only if it satisfies applicable statutes and regulations
f.statement: A Combination Product Applicant can use an approach other than the one in this guidance if the approach satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations; to discuss an alternative approach, the applicant can contact the FDA staff responsible for implementing the guidance.

rows.quote: You can use an alternative approach if the approach satisfies the requirements of the applicable statutes and regulations. If you want to discuss an alternative approach, contact the FDA staff responsible for implementing this guidance.

Double-check: quote proves the permission ('You can') and the contact route; Permitted correct. Below 90 because the actor is inferred: the preamble addresses 'you', and the guidance is directed to Combination Product Applicants (section I), so the actor is not in the quote. f.title: Determine whether the firm is a Combination Product Applicant or a Constituent Part Applicant
f.statement: The combination product PMSR final rule applies to combination products subject to premarket review by FDA. The entities subject to it are Combination Product Applicants (applicants that hold the only application for a combination product or all the applications for its constituent parts: drug, device or biological product) and Constituent Part Applicants (applicants for a constituent part of a combination product whose constituent parts are marketed under applications held by different applicants) (21 CFR 4.100, 4.101).
f.applicability: Combination products as defined at 21 CFR 3.2(e) that are subject to premarket review by FDA

rows.actor: Combination Product Applicant; Constituent Part Applicant
rows.quote: The combination product PMSR final rule applies to combination products that are subject to premarket review by FDA. The entities subject to the final rule are “Combination Product Applicants,” which are applicants that hold the only application for a combination product or all 1 the applications for the “constituent parts” (drug, device, or biological product) of a combination product, and “Constituent Part Applicants,” which are applicants for a constituent part of a combination product the constituent parts of which are marketed under applications held by different applicants (see 21 CFR 4.100 and 4.101).

The '1' in the quote is the page number at the page break, kept verbatim. Safety agreement owner consulted because Constituent Part Applicant status depends on applications held by different applicants. Double-check: kept only as a scope row, since applicant status (Combination Product Applicant vs Constituent Part Applicant) decides which 21 CFR Part 4 Subpart B duties apply. f.title: Comply with application type-based PMSR requirements for the combination product
f.statement: Under the combination product PMSR final rule, Combination Product Applicants must comply with application type-based postmarketing safety reporting requirements, i.e. the PMSR requirements associated with the application type under which the combination product received marketing authorization (21 CFR 4.102(a) and (b)).
f.processes: Reporting policy; Submission operations; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Under the final rule, Combination Product Applicants must comply with: application type-based PMSR requirements (PMSR requirements associated with the application type under which the combination product received marketing authorization) (see 21 CFR 4.102(a) and (b)),

Double-check: quote states the actor (Combination Product Applicants), the modal 'must comply with' and the 4.102(a)/(b) duty; statement adds nothing beyond it. Mandatory, actor, RACI and taxonomy confirmed.

f.title: Comply with constituent part-based PMSR, submission process and recordkeeping requirements
f.statement: Under the combination product PMSR final rule, Combination Product Applicants must also comply with constituent part-based PMSR requirements (specified in the rule based on the types of constituent parts included in the combination product; 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d)) and the associated submission process and recordkeeping requirements (21 CFR 4.104(b) and 4.105(b)).
f.exceptions: FDA does not intend to enforce 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d), 4.104(b)(1) and (b)(2), and 4.105(b) for Combination Product Applicants before July 31, 2020 (FAERS and eMDR users) or January 31, 2021 (VAERS users); see FDA-COMBO-PSR-2019-0006 and -0007.
f.processes: Reporting policy; Submission operations; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: Under the final rule, Combination Product Applicants must comply with: application type-based PMSR requirements (PMSR requirements associated with the application type under which the combination product received marketing authorization) (see 21 CFR 4.102(a) and (b)), constituent part-based PMSR requirements (specified in the rule based on the types of constituent parts included in the combination product) (see 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d)), and associated submission process and recordkeeping requirements (see 21 CFR 4.104(b) and 4.105(b)).

f.title: Comply with application type-based PMSR and Constituent Part Applicant submission/recordkeeping provisions from January 19, 2017
f.statement: The compliance date for the application type-based PMSR requirements for Combination Product Applicants and Constituent Part Applicants (21 CFR 4.102(a) and (b)), and for the submission process and recordkeeping requirements for Constituent Part Applicants (21 CFR 4.104(a) and 4.105(a)(1)), was the effective date of the final rule, January 19, 2017. These requirements are generally the same as for any other holder of such an application, and FDA expected all applicants subject to the rule to already be in compliance with them, since they generally refer to existing regulations that applicants have followed.

rows.actor: Combination Product Applicant; Constituent Part Applicant
rows.deadline: Compliance date January 19, 2017 (effective date of the final rule)
rows.quote: FDA stated that the compliance date for the application type-based PMSR requirements for Combination Product Applicants and Constituent Part Applicants under 21 CFR 4.102(a) and (b), and for the submission process and recordkeeping requirements for Constituent Part Applicants under 21 CFR 4.104(a) and 4.105(a)(1), respectively, was the same as the effective date for the final rule (January 19, 2017). These requirements are generally the same as for any other entity holding such an application for its product, and we expected all applicants subject to this rule to already be in compliance with these provisions as such provisions generally refer to existing regulations that such applicants have generally followed.
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory kept (flag ruled): the row records the binding compliance date of the final rule's requirements (a fact stated in the preamble, 81 FR at 92619), not a guidance recommendation; the date is when the 'must comply' duties of 0002 apply. Quote extended with the next sentence (FDA expected applicants to already be in compliance), statement updated to match; title reworded. No delayed enforcement applies to these provisions. Double-check: quote states the January 19, 2017 compliance date, the provisions (4.102(a)/(b) for both applicant types; 4.104(a), 4.105(a)(1) for Constituent Part Applicants) and both actors; statement faithful. Below 90: Mandatory for a compliance-date fact reported from the rule preamble is a judgement call (no modal verb in the guidance text).

f.title: Comply with 4.102(c)-(d), 4.103, 4.104(b) and 4.105(a)(2)-(b) from the July 19, 2018 compliance date
f.statement: For the PMSR requirements of 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d), 4.103, 4.104(b), and 4.105(a)(2) and (b), the final rule established a compliance date 18 months following the effective date of the rule, i.e. July 19, 2018.
f.exceptions: For Combination Product Applicants, FDA does not intend to enforce 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d), 4.104(b)(1) and (b)(2), and 4.105(b) before July 31, 2020 (FAERS and eMDR users) or January 31, 2021 (VAERS users); see FDA-COMBO-PSR-2019-0006 and -0007. 4.103 and 4.105(a)(2) are not covered by that policy.

rows.actor: Combination Product Applicant; Constituent Part Applicant

rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory kept (flag ruled): compliance date established by the final rule itself ('the final rule established a compliance date'), a binding fact. f.title: Delayed enforcement until July 31, 2020 for applicants reporting ICSRs via FAERS and eMDR
f.statement: FDA does not intend to enforce 21 CFR 4.102(c) and (d) (constituent part-based PMSR requirements), 4.104(b)(1) and (b)(2) (submission process for constituent part-based ICSRs) and 4.105(b) (recordkeeping requirements) prior to July 31, 2020, for Combination Product Applicants using FAERS and eMDR to report ICSRs.
f.clause: III. FDA's Compliance Policy for the Combination Product PMSR Final Rule
f.applicability: Combination Product Applicants using FAERS and eMDR to report ICSRs
f.processes: Reporting policy; Submission operations; Safety system configuration

f.title: Treat Fifteen-day, Five-day, Malfunction and death or serious injury reports as ICSRs under the combination product PMSR rule
f.statement: For purposes of the combination product PMSR final rule and this guidance, an ICSR is a report of an event experienced by an individual user of a combination product, including adverse events and malfunctions; ICSRs encompass Fifteen-day reports (21 CFR 314.80, 600.80), Five-day reports (21 CFR 803.3, 803.53, 803.56), Malfunction reports (21 CFR 803.50, 803.56), and death or serious injury reports (21 CFR Part 803).
f.clause: III. FDA's Compliance Policy for the Combination Product PMSR Final Rule, footnote 1 (ICSR definition)
f.processes: Reporting policy; Case processing & follow-up; Submission operations

rows.quote: The term “Individual Case Safety Report” (ICSR) is used to describe a report of an event experienced by an individual user of a combination product, including adverse events and malfunctions. For purposes of the combination product PMSR final rule and this guidance, ICSRs encompass Fifteen-day reports (see 21 CFR 314.80, 600.80), Five-day reports (see 21 CFR 803.3, 803.53, 803.56), Malfunction reports (see 21 CFR 803.50, 803.56), and death or serious injury reports (21 CFR Part 803).
rows.location: III. FDA's Compliance Policy for the Combination Product PMSR Final Rule, footnote 1 (ICSR definition)
data_elements: individual user of a combination product
rows.review_note: Review: kept as Recommended (flag ruled): the footnote defines which report types count as ICSRs for the rule and this guidance, i.e. which reports fall under the constituent part-based ICSR submission process (4.104(b)(1)/(b)(2)) and the delayed enforcement; nonbinding guidance wording, so Recommended. Deadline cleared: the quote names report types only and sets no clock; the 15-day/5-day clocks live in the cited regulations. Title made specific. Double-check: statement faithful to footnote 1 (ICSR definition and report types). Below 90: footnote-derived definition row; Recommended is a judgement call (it defines scope for the rule rather than stating 'should'); actor is inferred, the quote names none.

f.title: Comply with all other 21 CFR Part 4 Subpart B provisions: no delayed enforcement applies
f.statement: For all provisions of 21 CFR Part 4, Subpart B other than those under delayed enforcement (4.102(c) and (d), 4.104(b)(1) and (b)(2), and 4.105(b)), FDA intends to enforce the requirements per its usual enforcement policies, because FDA does not believe significant updates to systems and procedures are necessary to comply with these provisions.
f.clause: III. FDA's Compliance Policy for the Combination Product PMSR Final Rule
